title: LEFT + FIND: pull out a prefix

screens.prompt: In B6, extract the three-letter prefix from the reference in B2 (everything before the first dash).

hints.syntax: =LEFT(B2,FIND("-",B2)-1): FIND finds the dash, LEFT keeps what precedes it.
hints.func-left: LEFT works from the first character and needs a count of how many to keep.
hints.func-find: FIND supplies that count, so the prefix length never gets typed in.
hints.require-ref: Read B2; the other references are there for comparison.
hints.value: FIND returns 4, the dash position, so LEFT needs 3 characters. One more keeps the dash.
hints.error: The grader will say off by one when the dash survives: the answer is ORD, not ORD-.

reject.why: off by one: keeps the dash
off by one the other way: OR instead of ORD
takes the end of the reference
MID works here, but this lesson is about LEFT
hardcodes the length instead of locating the dash
no FIND, so the dash is never located
the prefix is typed, not extracted
reads the answer row instead of the reference in B2
FIND cannot locate a period in ORD-2024-0917

docs.explain:
FIND reports where a character sits inside a string, and LEFT takes a given number of characters from the start. Joined, they cut a prefix of any length off a code. The reference in B2 is ORD-2024-0917, so FIND("-",B2) returns 4, counting from one.

The dash is not part of the prefix, so the length is 4 minus 1. The formula =LEFT(B2,FIND("-",B2)-1) returns ORD in B6, and the minus one is the only thing keeping the dash out. Type the position FIND gave you and the answer comes back as ORD-.

LEFT(B2,3) gives the same answer on every row of this sheet, which is why it feels safe. It breaks the first time a code arrives with a four-letter prefix. FIND keeps the formula tied to the dash instead.

errors.text: The search string is absent from the cell, and FIND raises #VALUE! rather than returning 0.
LEFT(B2,FIND("-",B2)) keeps the dash, so the answer reads ORD- instead of ORD.
LEFT(B2,3) answers ORD here and drops the first letter of a four-letter prefix.

seo.title: LEFT and FIND in Excel: pull out a prefix
seo.description: FIND locates the dash and LEFT takes the text before it. FIND returns 4, so the length is 3 and the answer is ORD, not the whole reference.
